root_cause.text: The nf_conncount garbage-collection optimization in `net/netfilter/nf_conncount.c` skipped GC whenever it had already run in the same jiffy, without considering how many new connections were added, so under bursts of more than 8 tracked connections per jiffy the per-key list could not be cleaned fast enough and the connection limit was reached incorrectly.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `last_gc_count` to `struct nf_conncount_list` and changes the GC skip condition from `if ((u32)jiffies == list->last_gc)` to only skip when the GC already ran in the same jiffy **and** `(list->count - list->last_gc_count) < CONNCOUNT_GC_MAX_COLLECT`; it also raises the collection threshold from `CONNCOUNT_GC_MAX_NODES` (8) to `CONNCOUNT_GC_MAX_COLLECT` (64), matching the CVE text that says “If more than 8 new connections are tracked per jiffy the list won't be cleaned up fast enough possibly reaching the limit wrongly.”
